items.stem: What is meant by a solenoid?
items.answer: A coil of many circular turns of insulated copper wire wrapped closely in the shape of a cylinder

items.stem: The magnetic field at a distance of 5 cm from a long straight current-carrying wire is B. What will it be at 15 cm?
items.markingKey: (d) B ∝ 1/r for a straight wire, so increasing the distance 3 times makes the field 1/3.

items.stem: A long straight vertical wire carries current vertically downwards. What is the direction of the magnetic field at a point due south of the wire? How do the field lines look when seen from above?
items.answer: Towards the west; concentric circles, clockwise when seen from above
items.markingKey: Right-hand thumb rule: thumb along the current (vertically downwards); fingers curl clockwise (seen from above), so at a point to the south the field is towards the west.

items.stem: A long straight vertical wire carries current vertically upwards. What is the direction of the magnetic field at a point due east of the wire? How do the field lines look when seen from above?

items.stem: Define an electric motor.
items.answer: A device that converts electrical energy into mechanical energy

items.stem: A straight conductor carries current towards the west in a uniform magnetic field directed towards the north. Using Fleming's left-hand rule, find the direction of the force on the conductor.
items.markingKey: (d) Forefinger along the field (north), middle finger along the current (west); the thumb points vertically downwards.

items.stem: Why is a split ring commutator needed in a DC motor?
items.answer: It reverses the current in the coil after every half turn, so the force keeps rotating the coil in the same direction.
items.markingKey: 2 marks.

items.stem: Name the rule used to find the direction of force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field and state it.
items.answer: Fleming's left-hand rule: stretch the thumb, forefinger and middle finger of the left hand mutually perpendicular; forefinger along the field, middle finger along the current, thumb gives the force (motion).
items.markingKey: 1 mark name. 1 mark statement.

items.stem: A straight conductor carries current vertically upwards in a uniform magnetic field directed towards the north. Using Fleming's left-hand rule, find the direction of the force on the conductor.
items.markingKey: (a) Forefinger along the field (north), middle finger along the current (vertically upwards); the thumb points west.

items.stem: An electron beam moving horizontally towards the north enters a magnetic field directed vertically downwards. In which direction will the beam be deflected? (Current is opposite to the direction of electron flow.)
items.answer: The current is towards the south. By Fleming's left-hand rule (field downwards, current south), the force is towards the east, so the beam is deflected towards the east.
items.markingKey: 1 mark current direction. 1 mark rule. 1 mark answer.

items.stem: Why is the earth wire important for appliances like an electric iron or a refrigerator?
items.answer: If the live wire touches the metal body, current flows to the earth through the low-resistance earth wire, so the user does not get a severe shock.

items.stem:
Read: In a flat in Pune, a television (120 W) and a refrigerator (250 W) are plugged into the same 15 A circuit at 220 V. The metal bodies are connected to a green wire, and an MCB is fitted.
(i) Find the total current drawn. (ii) Is the circuit overloaded? (iii) What is the purpose of the green wire? (iv) How is an MCB better than a fuse wire?

items.markingKey: (c) B ∝ 1/r for a straight wire, so increasing the distance 3 times makes the field 1/3.

items.stem: An electric iron (1000 W), a toaster (800 W) and a refrigerator (250 W) are switched on together in a 220 V circuit with a 5 A fuse. Find the total current. Will the fuse blow?
items.markingKey: Total P = 2050 W; I = 2050/220 = 9.32 A, compared with 5 A.

items.stem: A straight conductor carries current towards the east in a uniform magnetic field directed towards the north. Using Fleming's left-hand rule, find the direction of the force on the conductor.
items.markingKey: (c) Forefinger along the field (north), middle finger along the current (east); the thumb points vertically upwards.
